job_description: CIPLC is looking for a qualified and hands-on  Executive – Health & Safety  to support HSE implementation across assigned EPC project sites. The role will be responsible for implementing the project HSE plan, conducting hazard identification and risk assessments, managing permit-to-work requirements, conducting safety inspections and toolbox talks, delivering HSE inductions and training, monitoring subcontractor compliance, investigating incidents and near-misses, and maintaining HSE records and reports. The position will also support emergency response, first aid, fire safety and other site safety requirements in coordination with project teams and relevant stakeholders. HSE Plan & Risk Management: Implement the project HSE plan, safety procedures and site rules at assigned project sites. Conduct hazard identification, risk assessments and Job Safety Analyses (JSA) for site activities. Ensure identified risk controls are implemented and maintained. Support the Assistant Manager – QA & Planning in monitoring overall site HSE compliance. Permit-to-work & Site Safety: Manage the Permit-to-Work system for work at height, hot work, lifting, excavation and electrical works including LOTO. Conduct daily safety inspections and toolbox talks. Ensure proper use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Monitor site activities and stop unsafe work when required. Monitor housekeeping, waste management, dust and noise control at site. Training & Emergency Preparedness: Deliver HSE induction for new workers, subcontractors and visitors. Organize safety training programs and emergency drills. Ensure first aid, fire safety and emergency response arrangements are available at site. Promote safety awareness among workers and project teams. Equipment & Worksite Inspection: Inspect lifting equipment, scaffolding, ladders, tools and fire extinguishers. Inspect temporary electrical installations and monitor electrical safety requirements. Monitor compliance with work-at-height, lifting and other high-risk activity requirements. Incident Investigation & Corrective Actions: Investigate incidents and near-misses and identify root causes. Follow up on corrective and preventive actions. Report HSE violations and monitor resolution. Maintain appropriate incident and corrective-action records. HSE Reporting & Documentation: Maintain HSE registers, man-hour and incident statistics. Maintain inspection reports and training records. Prepare weekly and monthly HSE reports for the Assistant Manager – QA & Planning and the client. Maintain accurate HSE documentation and statistics.

job_description: About the Organization Shakti Foundation for Disadvantaged Women (Shakti Foundation) is a national development organization and microfinance institution working across Bangladesh since 1992. The organization is committed to the socio-economic empowerment of disadvantaged women through social and financial inclusion. Beginning with a pilot urban microfinance program for slum-dwelling women in Dhaka, Shakti Foundation has strategically expanded its service network into rural areas and now serves more than 6 lac members through a nationwide network of 648 branches across 57 districts. Alongside microfinance, its programming spans health, climate change, financial inclusion and women’s empowerment, supported by an extensive field presence and community-based delivery platforms. Shakti is registered with the NGO Affairs Bureau of Bangladesh under the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Rules and with the Registrar of Joint Stock Companies and Firms under the Societies Registration Act 1860. It is also licensed by the Microcredit Regulatory Authority (MRA) to operate its microfinance program. Bangladesh faces escalating climate risks, including extreme heat, flooding, cyclones, salinity intrusion, water stress, ecosystem degradation and climate-sensitive health threats. These risks affect low-income women and other vulnerable populations disproportionately and can disrupt Shakti Foundation’s operations, assets, workforce, clients and service delivery. At the same time, Shakti Foundation’s reach creates opportunities to integrate climate resilience, environmental responsibility and low-carbon practices across programs and institutional systems. Under the Inclusive Climate Finance for Vulnerable Communities in Asia Pacific (ICCAP) program, Shakti Foundation intends to engage a qualified consultant or consulting firm to develop an organization-wide Climate Strategy and a practical Monitoring & Reporting Framework. The assignment will translate climate commitments into prioritized, costed and measurable actions, with clear governance, indicators, data tools, accountability and reporting arrangements. Project Context The Inclusive Climate Finance for Vulnerable Communities in the Asia Pacific (ICCAP) is a five-year regional project implemented by a consortium of three partners: Appui au Développement Autonome (ADA), the Asia Pacific Rural and Agricultural Credit Association (APRACA), and the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI). The project aims to improve and scale up access to both public and private climate finance flows through Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to vulnerable communities across the Asia-Pacific region, including Bangladesh, Bhutan, Cambodia, Fiji, Lao PDR, and Nepal. The project is financed by the International Climate Initiative (IKI) as part of the German Government’s international climate finance commitment. In Bangladesh, ADA is providing technical assistance to partner FSPs, including Shakti Foundation, to strengthen their capacity to integrate climate considerations into financial products, institutional strategies, operations, and monitoring systems. Under Work Package 2, Activity 1.2 of the ICCAP Technical Assistance Grant, Shakti Foundation will develop and implement a Board-approved Integrated Climate Strategy covering climate finance and green internal operations; a Shakti climate finance taxonomy aligned with the Bangladesh Green Taxonomy; and a monitoring and reporting system that is embedded in Shakti's core ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system and supported by a practical tracking tool for internal operations, with staff trained to use it. Objective The purpose of the consultancy is to provide Shakti Foundation with an evidence-based and implementable climate strategy, together with a monitoring and reporting system that enables the organization to plan, track, learn from and communicate its climate-related performance and results. Specifically, the consultancy will: Define a climate vision, strategic objectives and a 5-year roadmap aligned with Shakti’s institutional mission and its focus on women (Action 1.2.1). Develop an institutional climate finance taxonomy aligned with the Bangladesh Green Taxonomy and contextualized to Shakti Foundation’s target clients, priority sectors, financial products, and operational model (Action 1.2.2). Develop an internal Green Operations Strategy to strengthen Shakti Foundation’s environmental performance, with a focus on paper reduction, energy efficiency, waste management, and other relevant operational measures (Action 1.2.3). Facilitate stakeholder workshops, board presentation and formal approval of an Integrated Climate Strategy (Action 1.2.4). Establish a Climate Monitoring and Reporting Framework by defining standardized indicators for the climate portfolio covering climate finance and green internal operations, along with standardized reporting templates and practical data requirements (Action 1.2.5). Specify the data requirements for, and quality-assure, the integration of taxonomy and climate finance indicators into Shakti’s core ERP system by Shakti’s IT team (Action 1.2.6). Establish an Excel-based tracking system for internal green operations indicators to support regular data collection, monitoring, analysis, and reporting of Shakti Foundation’s environmental performance (Action 1.2.7). Strengthen institutional capacity by building the knowledge and skills of relevant Shakti Foundation staff to implement the Climate Strategy and M&R Framework, collect and manage climate-related data, track indicators and effectively use reporting tools and dashboards (Action 1.2.8). Expected Outputs Inception Report, including the detailed work plan and allocation of professional days. Board-approved Integrated Climate Strategy for Shakti, incorporating climate finance vision, objectives and strategic roadmap. Shakti Climate Finance Taxonomy aligned with the Bangladesh Green Taxonomy, with loan categorization codes, ERP tags, application guidance, product mapping, pilot results and an indicative portfolio estimate. Internal Green Operations Strategy with baseline assessment, targets, costed measures and green office guidelines. Stakeholder Consultation Reports and Board Presentation. Climate Monitoring and Reporting Framework, including indicator reference sheets and three core reporting templates. ERP Data Requirements Specification, test scenarios and ERP Integration Review Note. Tested Excel Internal Operations Tracking Tool and User Guide. SOP Manual, Training Materials and Training-of-Trainers Completion Report with cascade plan. Final Assignment Report and Handover Package. Duration and Working Modality Duration:  6 months from contract signing Work Approach: Evidence-Based Assessment: Conduct comprehensive desk reviews, data-gap assessments, and climate risk/vulnerability analyses that merge credible secondary data with institutional and community-level experiences. Participatory Engagement & Co-Design: Facilitate key-informant interviews, field visits, and focused co-design sessions across all levels—from frontline staff and community stakeholders to program/support functions—to ensure deep institutional ownership of the strategy and monitoring frameworks. Iterative Development & Testing: Utilize a feedback-driven process to draft, validate, and practically pilot-test strategies, monitoring indicators, and tools before finalization. Capacity Building: Deliver targeted training and capacity-building initiatives to ensure the organization can seamlessly implement and sustain the new frameworks. Ethical & Inclusive Integration: Mainstream gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, "do-no-harm" principles, data protection, and ethical participation throughout all phases of the assignment. Alignment by design: outputs are developed against international climate finance conventions from the outset, so that they remain usable as Shakti's funding base widens, without substantial rework. Field Requirements: Field engagement at selected branches is required for the operations baseline, pilot testing and staff training.  শাখার সার্বিক কার্যক্রম পর্যালোচনা করা। পূর্ববর্তী পরিদর্শনে দেওয়া নির্দেশনার বাস্তবায়ন অগ্রগতি যাচাই করা এবং প্রয়োজনীয় ফলোআপ নিশ্চিত করা। ২. সমিতি ও মাঠ পর্যায় পরিদর্শন নিয়মিত সমিতি পরিদর্শনের
